source.cells: SFM 150; Chip load .00003; ADOC .14 x Dia; RDOC 1 x Dia

vendor_notes: All posted speed and feed parameters are suggested starting values that may be increased given optimal setup conditions.
Chip loads reflect uncoated cutters and may be increased 10%-20% if coated.
For ferrous materials with hardness <= 28 Rc, chip loads can be increased 10%-20%.
WARNING: Cutting tools may shatter under improper use. Government regulations require use of safety glasses and other appropriate safety equipment in the vicinity of use.
rows.notes: Group also contains martensitic 414, 431, 440A/B/C; values are shared by all alloys in the group. Values read from pdftotext -raw (clean row text) and cross-checked against the rendered page. Chart diameter column mapped to the Harvey part whose DC equals the column header. Chart chip-load row labels (Slotting/Roughing/Finishing) share one SFM per material group.

rows.notes: Harvey sells these as "Variable Helix End Mills for High Temp Alloys"; variable_pitch=true inferred from the product name (tool page does not list helix/pitch). Coating code C6 = AlTiN Nano per Harvey tool-coatings page. Checked against rendered page 1 (pdftoppm 105 dpi): column header, material/hardness row and DOC columns all agree with the text layer. The sheet prints no pair of small/large-diameter DOC values: Radial/Axial DOC are fixed per operation row (Slotting/Roughing/Finishing) for all diameters. Chart also lists a 'Max' chip-load row for this diameter (.00011); it is a cap, not an operation, and is not emitted. Inconel 718 mapped to the 'Nickel Alloys' group; the 350-400 HBn band was chosen as the age-hardened condition (~38-43 HRC, approximate conversion not printed); existing repo rows for SF_875400 use the 300-350 band (SFM 60) - chip loads are identical across hardness bands, only SFM changes.

source.cells: Hard/Ferrous Materials: 1°-3°

vendor_notes: Suggested STARTING values; vendor refers users to Machining Advisor Pro / Milling Advisor for application-specific entry parameters.
Corner-radius end mills are recommended by the vendor for ramping and helical interpolation.
Straight plunge: 'least preferred method and one that can easily break a tool; tool must be center cutting' (no numeric value published).
Straight entry / roll-in entry: reduce feed rate by at least 50% / by 50% (radial entry into full engagement, not an axial ramp; not encoded).
rows.notes: Series-wide rule: the vendor prints no per-diameter or per-series ramp data, so the same published rule is replicated over representative diameters (1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 in) and material families; treat the replicas as ONE independent observation per rule when calibrating. Vendor text says 'Hard/Ferrous Materials' and 'Soft/Non-Ferrous Materials' only; the mapping of the ferrous group to the toolwiz family (17-4 PH / H13 / 4130) is the row builder's, not the vendor's. Part number and catalog geometry from the product page (see geometry_url): corner radius 0 = 'Profile: Square'; helix angle not printed except H45AL-3 (45 deg in product title). The angle is a 'suggested starting' range, not a maximum; the vendor does not say whether it applies to linear or helical ramps (the guidebook's Ramping-In picture is a linear ramp; the Ramping section p.6 and the 'Ramping to Success' blog treat 'circular or linear' together), so kind='any'. Corroborated by the Helical Solutions Machining Guidebook (c)2016 p.4 with identical ranges and by the 'Ramping to Success' blog (2017-05-10). Vendor also recommends corner-radius end mills and a tool with good core strength for ramping; this row is a square end mill.

source.cells: use a programmed helix diameter of greater than 110-120% of the cutter diameter
